title: Lowe’s Red Vests Help Refresh Oklahoma City Homeless Shelter
summary: Lowe’s Red Vests Help Refresh Oklahoma City Homeless Shelter
body_markdown:
Sometimes making a place feel more like home starts with something as simple as a place to sit.


At City Care in Oklahoma City, that means giving someone a place to rest,


take


a breath and


feel


welcome.


“To be able to have a place to sit seems so simple, but it’s a place to rest and a place for them to just take a minute and take a breather and to just have a spot outside the doors to feel welcome,”


Kesli


Dye, volunteer coordinator of City Care said.


City Care operates a 140-bed, low-barrier shelter for people experiencing homelessness. Its mission is to create a community where people can find safety,


belonging


and a place to call home.


Recently, Lowe’s associates stepped in to help make that mission a little easier.


Red Vests volunteered at the shelter, taking on projects including painting and refreshing spaces throughout the property.


“City Care is part of our community,” said


Amber Leach, assistant store manager in Oklahoma City.


“It’s a huge resource for the people that live in this area.


So


we’re able to come in and knock out the painting to refresh their community and make this feel like more of a home for them.”


For a small nonprofit, having community partners take on that work means City Care can keep its attention where it matters most: its guests.


“Having Lowe’s show up this way allows City Care to really focus on our guests and really providing them with the services that we have here,” communications manager of city care,


Brooke Kuwitzky,


said.


“We


want to treat all of our guests with care and dignity and make them feel like they have worth and value.”


The work also wasn't meant to be a one-day relationship.


“It doesn’t stop here,” said Lowe’s assistant store manager Ty Mustin. “We’re still going to keep on reaching out, seeing what they need. They have our back, we have their backs, and that’s what the community does.”


By the end of the day, fresh paint and updated spaces were visible signs of what had changed. But for the City Care team, the real measure of the work would come later, when guests walked through the doors.


“I hope that the guests who come in tonight can feel that this is somewhere where we take a lot of pride in making it a space that is beautiful and that feels safe and warm and somewhere where they can start new.”
